text:
samira: hey folks, accepted the GitHub invite but can't open private repos in VS Code. The GH extension prompts for a token and then shows 403. In browser the org page says 'SAML SSO: authorization required'.
leo: did you accept with your work account? VS Code's extension sometimes caches a different account and shows the token dialog for that one.
samira: accepted with samira@redwood.ai. In the browser I can see the org banner asking to authorize SSO but there's no button visible in the embedded VS Code window.
people-ops: onboarding tip: after accepting the invite you must click "Authorize SSO" on https://github.com/orgs/redwood while signed into your work account. If a GUI client opens an embedded browser, open that same URL in your normal browser and finish the SSO flow there.
dev-tools-bot: dev-tools: check-list -> confirm work email verified, authorize SSO, ensure SSH key attached to work account, or generate a personal access token with repo scope if using HTTPS from a GUI client.
samira: my work email wasn't verified on GitHub. It was listed but unverified. I can't find the verification mail in Inbox.
maria: sometimes corporate mail filters hide GH verification. People-ops can resend or you can add a secondary and re-invite.
people-ops: resent verification and reissued the org invite. Heads up: we recommend verifying work email before accepting to avoid account merge problems.
samira: ok verified and accepted again. Still no Authorize SSO button in normal Chrome (adblock + privacy extensions enabled). Incognito shows the button. Clicked it, redirected to Okta for approval and SSO completed.
leo: next step for VS Code: sign out of the GitHub extension (Command Palette -> Sign out), then sign in again; that will open the browser and pick up the SSO session.
samira: signed in via VS Code after SSO and browser got me prompted. Now the GH extension shows my org repos but when I try to push I get "remote: Permission to redwood/apps.git denied to samira (use a personal access token)".
maria: that message suggests VS Code is trying HTTPS with a cached credential helper rather than SSH. `git remote -v` shows URLs. If it's https://github.com/... you either need a PAT or switch to SSH.
samira: remote is https. I prefer SSH. I checked Settings -> SSH and GPG keys, my SSH key was only on my personal account.
people-ops: (typo fix) people-ops: quick note: make sure ssh key is tied to the work account. If you move keys between accounts, remove from personal first to avoid surprises.
leo: also run `ssh-add -l` and `ssh -T git@github.com` to verify agent and greeting. If your key is passphrase-protected, ensure the agent has it loaded or VS Code may fall back to HTTPS.
samira: added my key to work account, did `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` and `ssh -T` returns "Hi samira! You've successfully authenticated..." Pushed a tiny branch and it worked.
dev-tools-bot: dev-tools: resolution noted -> cause: unverified work email + VS Code cached session + SSH key on personal account. Advice: verify email first, authorize SSO in browser, re-login in GUI clients, attach SSH key to work account.
people-ops: thanks for reporting steps. We'll add a short onboarding blurb: "If using VS Code/GitHub Desktop, authorize SSO in your default browser first, then reauthenticate GUI clients; ensure SSH key attached to work account or use a PAT with repo scope for HTTPS." Welcome to the team, @samira :tada:
samira: thanks everyone — leaving a short note in the onboarding doc with exact commands I used so future folks hit fewer roadblocks.
